market_context: United States/general English; raw walnuts and pistachios compared per 100 g and roughly 1-ounce serving
title: Walnuts vs. pistachios: nutrition differences

seo.title: Walnuts vs. pistachios: protein, fiber, fat, omega-3
seo.meta_description: Pistachios provide more protein and fiber with fewer calories; walnuts stand out for ALA omega-3. Compare equal 100 g and 1-ounce-style servings.
seo.search_intent: Compare walnuts and pistachios for calories, protein, fiber, fat and omega-3 at equal weights.

excerpt: Pistachios clearly lead in protein and fiber by equal weight; walnuts lead even more dramatically in ALA, the main plant omega-3. A 1-ounce-style serving gives about 6 grams protein from pistachios versus roughly 4.5 grams from walnuts, while walnuts deliver around 2.6 grams ALA.
content_html:
Walnuts and pistachios are both nuts, but their nutrition profiles solve different problems. Pistachios are higher in protein and fiber; walnuts are dramatically higher in ALA, the main plant omega-3.

Per 100 grams

NutrientWalnutsPistachios
Calories~654~560
Protein~15.2 g~20.2 g
Fat~65.2 g~45.3 g
Fiber~6.7 g~10.6 g
ALA~9.1 g~0.3 g

Pistachios provide about 5 g more protein and 3.9 g more fiber per 100 g, with about 94 fewer calories. Walnuts provide roughly 8.8 g more ALA.

At a 30 g serving

Thirty grams of walnuts is about 196 calories, 4.6 g protein, 2.0 g fiber, and roughly 2.7 g ALA. The same weight of pistachios is about 168 calories, 6.1 g protein, 3.2 g fiber, and less than 0.1 g ALA.

That means pistachios save about 28 calories and add roughly 1.5 g protein, while walnuts add more than 2.5 g ALA.

Why walnuts are higher in calories

Fat is the main reason: roughly 65 g/100 g versus 45 g/100 g. That is about 20 g additional fat per 100 g, while the final calorie difference is around 94 calories because all macronutrients contribute to the full composition.

Walnut omega-3 is ALA

NIH lists 2.57 g ALA in 1 oz of English walnuts. That makes walnuts one of the most concentrated everyday ALA foods. It should not be read as 2.57 g EPA+DHA because conversion of ALA to the long-chain forms is limited.

Pistachios lead on protein, fiber, and potassium

At about 20.2 g protein and 10.6 g fiber per 100 g, pistachios are well above walnuts for both. They also provide substantially more potassium by equal weight.

Which one should you choose?

If ALA is the goal, walnuts have an enormous advantage. If you want more protein and fiber with somewhat fewer calories, pistachios fit those numbers better. Both are rich in unsaturated fat and can easily coexist in a varied diet.

The useful takeaway

Walnuts and pistachios do not have the same nutritional specialty. Walnuts stand out for ALA; pistachios provide more protein and fiber for fewer calories at the same weight.

faq.question: Which has more protein, walnuts or pistachios?
faq.answer: Pistachios: about 20.2 g/100 g versus 15.2 g in walnuts. At 30 g, that is roughly 6.1 versus 4.6 g.

faq.question: Which has more omega-3?
faq.answer: Walnuts by a very large margin, providing about 2.6–2.7 g ALA in a 28–30 g serving.

faq.question: Which has fewer calories?
faq.answer: Pistachios, at roughly 560 calories/100 g versus 654 for walnuts.
